requirements.requirement: Repair and operate the local service at /srv/legacy2/unix-socket-access-boundary/run/status.sock, including recovery after node restart.
requirements.summary: The service ran as statusd on the required Unix socket before restart. A reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the service, process, socket, and client response recovered afterward. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

requirements.requirement: Limit service access to the statusd service owner and members of status-readers, and provision status-reader and outsider accounts with the appropriate roles.
requirements.summary: The required accounts and group exist with status-reader included and outsider excluded. The service runs as statusd; the socket is statusd:status-readers mode 0660, authorized identities connect successfully, and outsider receives permission denied both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Return the supplied status document for exactly STATUS followed by a newline and return an error for other requests.
requirements.summary: Authorized STATUS requests returned the supplied two-line document. A non-STATUS newline-terminated request returned ERROR before and after reboot; the installed source shown in the mutation command also implements the exact request comparison and error branch.
The final and post-restart SHA-256 matches the prepared baseline hash, and the returned content remains branch=west and state=ready.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged after implementation and reboot. The service ran successfully with the installed Python 2.4.3 and CentOS SysV service infrastructure.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional and access-control tests. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and internally consistent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, observed unavailability, a changed boot identity, and recovered service, data, protocol, and authorization state. The only notable deficiency is uncleaned temporary staging, test, and reboot-log residue.
limitations: The lifecycle package-health probe invokes an unsupported yum operation on this legacy release, so it does not establish package consistency; no package mutations appear in the executor timeline.
Only one representative invalid request was exercised directly, although the captured installed implementation shows all requests other than exact STATUS followed by newline taking the ERROR branch.
The lifecycle failed-service probe is unavailable because this CentOS 5 platform does not use systemd.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation mutations were causally related to the task, and the initial account-provisioning attempt did not change state because its administrative commands were unavailable. Hygiene is reduced by five executor-created temporary artifacts left behind: staged server source and compiled bytecode from cmd-6c60e1c3136c4db4, staged init script from cmd-12b3a9d14ad84b6a, test client from cmd-9f98c271937f472f, and reboot log from cmd-a3085b5c0a714f94. These remained after execution rather than being cleaned up. No unnecessary package, OS, or network exposure changes are evidenced.
